hints: Determine which graph is above the other over the interval $1 \le x \le 16$: the line $y = x - 16$ lies above the curve $y = 5x^{3/2} - 20x$.
Set up the definite integral for the area: $\text{Area} = \int_1^{16} \left((x - 16) - (5x^{3/2} - 20x)\right) dx = \int_1^{16} \left(21x - 16 - 5x^{3/2}\right) dx$.
Integrate each term using the power rule: $\int 21x dx = \frac{21}{2}x^2$, $\int -16 dx = -16x$, and $\int -5x^{3/2} dx = -2x^{5/2}$.
Evaluate the antiderivative $\left[\frac{21}{2}x^2 - 16x - 2x^{5/2}\right]$ at limits $16$ and $1$ and subtract.
walkthrough:
Identify that the straight line $y = x - 16$ lies above the curve $y = 5x^{3/2} - 20x$ on $[1, 16]$, and set up the area integral:
$$\text{Area} = \int_1^{16} \left((x - 16) - (5x^{3/2} - 20x)\right) dx = \int_1^{16} \left(21x - 16 - 5x^{3/2}\right) dx$$

Integrate term-by-term with respect to $x$:
$$\int \left(21x - 16 - 5x^{3/2}\right) dx = \left[ \frac{21}{2}x^2 - 16x - 5 \times \frac{x^{5/2}}{5/2} \right]_1^{16} = \left[ \frac{21}{2}x^2 - 16x - 2x^{5/2} \right]_1^{16}$$

Evaluate the integrated expression at the upper limit $x = 16$:
$$\text{At } x = 16: \quad \frac{21}{2}(256) - 16(16) - 2(16)^{5/2} = 2688 - 256 - 2(1024) = 2688 - 256 - 2048 = 384$$

Evaluate the integrated expression at the lower limit $x = 1$:
$$\text{At } x = 1: \quad \frac{21}{2}(1) - 16(1) - 2(1)^{5/2} = 10.5 - 16 - 2 = -7.5 = -\frac{15}{2}$$

Subtract the lower limit value from the upper limit value:
$$\text{Area} = 384 - \left(-\frac{15}{2}\right) = 384 + 7.5 = 391.5 = \frac{783}{2}$$
